*   **Strengths:** Excellent normal accuracy for nearly planar surfaces; exactly reproduces 2D lines; significantly reduces aliasing patterns and ridges compared to MC [S1].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. 1. 'Excellent normal accuracy for nearly planar surfaces': The text states, 'Our contour is very accurate for nearly planar surfaces (spheres with large radii)' and notes that for spheres with radius 15+, the maximum normal error is 'as good as or better than the average error for surfaces produced by MC.' 2. 'Exactly reproduces 2D lines': The text explicitly states, 'Our algorithm exactly reproduces two dimensional lines.' 3. 'Significantly reduces aliasing patterns and ridges compared to MC': The text mentions that 'ridges in the surface are greatly reduced in our surface compared to MC' and that 'ripple patterns produced by Marching Cubes... are especially obvious compared to our method,' which refers to aliasing patterns.
supported
"""Selects one of four cases based on occupancies relative to threshold [S1]."""

Thus, the selection of the four cases is directly linked to the occupancies relative to the threshold.

It sets itself apart from [Marching Cubes 2](1393-marching-cubes-2.md) by replacing standard linear interpolation with a reduction of the 3D problem to a 2D case, which exactly preserves 2D line areas and significantly reduces normal error and volume deviation for planar surfaces [S1].

The claim states that the method replaces standard linear interpolation with a reduction of the 3D problem to a 2D case. The evidence confirms this, stating 'Unlike Marching Cubes which uses linear interpolation, this method uses a 2D reduction'. The claim states this 'exactly preserves 2D line areas'. The evidence confirms: 'Our algorithm exactly reproduces two dimensional lines' and 'In 2D, we exactly preserve areas of lines'. The claim states it 'significantly reduces normal error and volume deviation for planar surfaces'. The evidence supports this with specific data: for normal error, 'for a sphere with a radius of fifteen cells or more, even the maximum error from our method is as good as or better than the average error for surfaces produced by MC'; for volume deviation, 'The standard deviation of the difference in reconstructed volumes... was 2.76% for MC, whereas the standard deviation was only 0.07% for our method' and 'The average absolute difference in volume was 8.36% for MC and only 0.46% for our method'.
supported
